purpose.text: Provide a toolkit for analyzing website traffic, content performance, audiences, engagement, conversions, e-commerce revenue, live activity, and period comparisons in GA4; analyze organic search performance in Search Console; inspect URL index status and submit requested indexing notifications; and make analysis results available for review and Markdown summaries.

evidences.reason: Identifies the services and the website analytics, SEO, and indexing purposes.
Defines the workflow from API analysis through saved results to a human-readable summary.
Distinguishes requests to recrawl or remove URLs from inspection of their status.

requirements.text: Set up the toolkit with its npm dependencies installed in the scripts directory and use Node.js 18 or later.

evidences.reason: Prescribes dependency installation in the scripts directory.
The setup script installs dependencies from its own directory.
Declares the supported minimum Node.js version.

requirements.text: For full toolkit setup, enable the Analytics Data, Search Console, and Indexing APIs in the Google Cloud project and use a service account with access to the target GA4 property and Search Console site. Configure the property ID, service account email and private key, and Search Console site URL through the project environment.

evidences.reason: Names the configuration values, enabled APIs, and service account access prerequisites.
Shows the environment settings used for the service account and target resources.
Connects the credentials to the GA4 client and the configured property ID to GA4 requests.
Uses the service account for Search Console and Indexing authentication.

requirements.text: For GA4 reports that take a date range, accept an Nd shorthand ending today, an explicit start and end date, or GA4 relative start and end values. When an optional range is omitted, use GA4_DEFAULT_DATE_RANGE with a default of 30d.

evidences.reason: Describes the three date representations and the configurable default.
Shows how shorthand is interpreted and how explicit or relative date objects are passed through.
Supplies the configured setting and its fallback.

requirements.text: For dated Search Console analytics, accept Nd shorthand through today or a pair of calendar dates. Send both dates in YYYY-MM-DD format, using GA4_DEFAULT_DATE_RANGE with a default of 30d when the range is omitted.

evidences.reason: Describes shorthand, explicit dates, and the configurable default at toolkit level.
States the Search Console date format, uses the settings default, and converts shorthand to calendar dates.
Shows that the parsed date pair is used for the Search Console query.

requirements.text: Run a custom report for the configured GA4 property using the caller's selected dimension and metric names and the applicable date range. Return report rows with the dimension and metric values associated within each row.

evidences.reason: Specifies the caller-selected report fields, date range, and row result.
Defines the association of dimension and metric values in each report row.

requirements.text: Apply caller-supplied dimension filters to a custom GA4 report when those filters are specified.

evidences.reason: Documents optional dimension filters as part of the custom report interface.

requirements.text: Respect a caller-supplied sort order for a custom GA4 report when it is specified.

evidences.reason: Documents an optional sort order for the custom report.

requirements.text: Apply the optional row limit for a custom GA4 report when one is specified.

evidences.reason: Documents the row limit as a separate custom report option.
Shows the report request carrying the row limit when populated.

requirements.text: Report screenPageViews, activeUsers, and averageSessionDuration grouped by pagePath and pageTitle for the requested GA4 period.

evidences.reason: Specifies the page-view report's grouping, measures, and date input.

requirements.text: Report sessions, activeUsers, newUsers, and bounceRate grouped by sessionSource, sessionMedium, and sessionCampaignName for the requested GA4 period.

evidences.reason: Specifies the traffic-source grouping and measures, including bounce rate.

requirements.text: Report activeUsers, sessions, and newUsers grouped by country, deviceCategory, and browser for the requested GA4 period.

evidences.reason: Defines the audience breakdown and the metrics to report.

requirements.text: Report eventCount, eventCountPerUser, and activeUsers grouped by eventName for the requested GA4 period.

evidences.reason: Defines event names as the grouping and specifies the event measures.

requirements.text: Report conversions and totalRevenue grouped by eventName and sessionSource for the requested GA4 period.

evidences.reason: Defines the conversion report's measures and breakdown.

requirements.text: Report totalRevenue, ecommercePurchases, and averagePurchaseRevenue by date and transactionId for the requested GA4 period.

evidences.reason: Specifies the e-commerce measures and explicitly includes transaction-level breakdown.

requirements.text: For a comprehensive site overview, combine page views, traffic sources, demographics, and event counts for the same date range.

evidences.reason: Names the four components of the site snapshot.
Passes the same date-range input to the four components.

requirements.text: For a traffic analysis, include the traffic-source report; sessions, engagedSessions, averageSessionDuration, and bounceRate by sessionSource and sessionMedium; and activeUsers, sessions, and conversions by newVsReturning. Use the same date range for these components.

evidences.reason: Names the source, session, and new-versus-returning views in the traffic analysis.
Specifies the component measures and their shared date range.

requirements.text: For content performance, include the page-view report, sessions, activeUsers, bounceRate, and averageSessionDuration by landingPage, and exits and screenPageViews by pagePath, all for the same date range.

evidences.reason: Identifies page views, landing pages, and exit pages as the content analysis components.
Specifies the landing and exit measures and applies the common date range.

requirements.text: For a user behavior analysis, include demographics, events, and daily activeUsers, engagedSessions, engagementRate, and averageSessionDuration for the same date range.

evidences.reason: Identifies demographics, events, and daily engagement as the behavior analysis components.
Specifies the daily engagement measures and common date range.

requirements.text: Compare two supplied GA4 date ranges side by side. Use the same dimensions and metrics for both, defaulting to date and the metrics activeUsers, sessions, and screenPageViews. Keep each result paired with its own supplied date range, in the caller's period order.

evidences.reason: Calls for side-by-side metrics for two date ranges.
Uses the same fields for both reports and pairs each response with its original date range.

requirements.text: Provide a current GA4 snapshot containing active user counts, currently viewed pages or screens, and current event counts.

evidences.reason: Defines the three components of the realtime snapshot.
Collects the three current reports without a historical date input.

requirements.text: For granular realtime reporting, provide activeUsers by unifiedScreenName, eventCount by eventName, screenPageViews by unifiedScreenName, and activeUsers by firstUserSource and firstUserMedium through their respective operations.

evidences.reason: Defines the four distinct realtime reports and their breakdowns.
Identifies activeUsers as the measure for current users by screen.
Identifies screenPageViews as the measure for the current page report.

requirements.text: List all available dimensions and metrics for the configured GA4 property. Support listing either collection on its own, with each entry's API name, display name, and description.

evidences.reason: Defines the utility as listing all available GA4 dimensions and metrics.
Defines separate dimension and metric retrieval and the information supplied for each entry.
Shows the property-specific requests and the corresponding named collections.

requirements.text: When full GA4 property metadata is requested, return the full property metadata response, including both the dimension and metric collections.

evidences.reason: Explicitly specifies the full metadata response for this operation.
Returns the full response from the configured property's metadata request.

requirements.text: Query analytics for the configured Search Console site. Support caller-selected dimensions, a date range, a row limit, and a starting row. Default to the query dimension, a maximum of 1,000 rows, and starting row zero. Return the dimension keys with their corresponding clicks, impressions, click-through rate, and position in each result row.

evidences.reason: Specifies the query controls, their defaults, and the fields of a result row.
Shows the query controls applied to the configured Search Console site.

requirements.text: Return up to 100 top Search Console queries by clicks for the applicable date range.

evidences.reason: Specifies the query breakdown, count, and ranking criterion.
Selects the query dimension and caps the returned rows at 100.

requirements.text: Return up to 100 top page rows for the applicable Search Console date range. The criterion for ranking the shared page operation has conflicting descriptions.

evidences.reason: Defines a top-100 page report and describes ranking by impressions.
Selects the page dimension and a 100-row limit without selecting an explicit ordering criterion.
Describes the same standalone page operation as ranking by clicks.

requirements.text: Report Search Console performance broken down by device type for the applicable date range.

evidences.reason: Defines device type as the requested breakdown.

requirements.text: Report Search Console performance for up to 50 top countries in the applicable date range.

evidences.reason: Defines the country breakdown and the top-50 scope.
Applies a 50-row cap to the country breakdown.

requirements.text: Report Search Console performance broken down by search appearance for the applicable date range.

evidences.reason: Defines the search appearance report and its date input.

requirements.text: For a Search Console overview, combine top queries, top pages, device performance, and country performance for the same date range.

evidences.reason: Specifies the four parts of the SEO snapshot.
Uses the same date-range input for the four search components.

requirements.text: For keyword analysis, provide top queries and a device breakdown for the same Search Console date range.

evidences.reason: Calls for queries with a device breakdown in the keyword analysis.
Collects top queries and device performance using the same date range.

requirements.text: For SEO page performance, provide a top-pages view described as ranking by clicks, together with a country breakdown for the same Search Console date range.

evidences.reason: Specifies top pages by clicks and a country breakdown for this analysis.
Labels the page view as ranked by clicks and invokes both the shared top-pages and country operations.

requirements.text: For bulk GA4 page lookup, trim whitespace from each supplied page path, add a leading slash when absent, and preserve a trailing slash when present.

evidences.reason: Defines the inputs as page paths and calls for whitespace trimming and a leading slash.
Explicitly preserves trailing slashes while normalizing each path.

requirements.text: For a nonempty bulk lookup, report metrics for the requested normalized page paths using case-insensitive membership on pagePath. Keep the returned metrics associated with their page path and title. Use caller-selected metrics when supplied; otherwise report screenPageViews, activeUsers, averageSessionDuration, bounceRate, and engagementRate.

evidences.reason: Specifies the path filter, bulk lookup purpose, per-page result, and default metrics.
Defines the filter as case-insensitive membership on pagePath.
Uses the normalized path filter, the selected metrics, and page path and title as the dimensions.

requirements.text: For an empty bulk path list, return no rows and a row count of zero without issuing an unfiltered GA4 report or saving a report for that lookup. The standalone filter builder returns null for an empty list.

evidences.reason: Specifies the filter builder's result when no paths are supplied.
Returns the empty result before preparing the API request or reaching the save step.

requirements.text: For a single full URL supplied for recrawling, submit a URL_UPDATED notification to Google and return its URL, notification type, and notification time.

evidences.reason: Specifies the full URL input, recrawl purpose, notification type, and receipt fields.
Shows the submitted URL and the corresponding update receipt.

requirements.text: For the low-level batch recrawl operation, process the supplied URLs sequentially and return their notification receipts in the same order on success.

evidences.reason: Requires sequential processing to avoid rate limits and returns an array of notification results.
Awaits each URL in order and appends each completed receipt to the batch result.

requirements.text: For high-level reindexing, attempt each supplied URL and return its individual submission or failure status. Preserve the corresponding notification details on success and error information on failure, and continue to the later URLs after an individual failure.

evidences.reason: Defines the high-level operation as requesting reindexing for multiple URLs.
Associates each outcome with its URL and handles failures within the loop so later URLs are attempted.

requirements.text: For a URL supplied to the removal operation, submit a URL_DELETED notification to Google and return its URL, notification type, and notification time.

evidences.reason: Defines the removal request and its notification receipt.
Shows the supplied URL in the deletion notification and constructs the associated receipt.

requirements.text: Inspect the supplied URL against the configured Search Console site. Report its index verdict and coverage state, and include last crawl time, mobile usability, and rich result findings when available.

evidences.reason: Defines the inspection's purpose and names the index, crawl, usability, and rich result information.
Uses the supplied inspection URL and configured site together and retains the applicable inspection findings.

requirements.text: Check index status for each supplied URL, keeping each URL associated with its own status. Set the indexed flag for a PASS verdict; when inspection fails, return a false flag with error details and continue checking the remaining URLs.

evidences.reason: Defines the high-level status check for multiple URLs.
Defines the per-URL status, the PASS condition, and the handling of an individual inspection failure.

requirements.text: Automatically save report results by default as timestamped JSON in the appropriate category under results. For an operation with a documented save option, honor an explicit false value by returning the result without saving it.

evidences.reason: Makes automatic JSON persistence a stage of analysis.
Identifies the standard result categories and the separate summaries location.
Documents the report save option and its default.
Documents the same opt-out for metadata operations.
Identifies metadata as a result category and saves full metadata only when enabled.
Documents the Search Console save option and its default.
Documents the default save option for indexing and inspection operations.
Documents the independent save option for bulk GA4 lookup.
Documents the default save behavior for the realtime reports.

requirements.text: Save the completed comparison and the high-level indexing and inspection results as combined artifacts without saving their component calls separately. The low-level batch recrawl likewise saves the combined receipts, when saving is enabled, rather than a file per notification.

evidences.reason: Disables component saves for both comparison periods and saves the assembled comparison.
Disables single-URL saves during reindexing and saves the combined outcomes.
Disables individual inspection saves and saves the combined statuses.
Disables per-URL saving during low-level batch recrawl and applies the save option to the batch artifact.

requirements.text: Use YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS followed by the operation name for a saved JSON filename, with double underscores as separators and an extra information segment only when one is provided. Place the file in the requested result category and return its full path from the save utility.

evidences.reason: Specifies timestamped JSON under a result category and names the filename segments.
Specifies the category, operation, optional extra filename information, and returned path.
Shows the timestamped filename and conditional inclusion of the extra segment.

requirements.text: When saving a result, put the result data in a JSON wrapper with its save timestamp, category, operation, configured GA4 property ID, and extra information when supplied.

evidences.reason: Specifies saving the supplied result data in a metadata wrapper.
Declares the wrapper's data and metadata fields and marks extra information as optional.
Shows the association of the saved data with the metadata for that file.

requirements.text: Load the previously saved JSON result at the supplied file path; return null when the file does not exist or cannot be read or parsed.

evidences.reason: Defines loading by path and permits a null result.
Defines the missing-file and read or parse failure cases.

requirements.text: List saved JSON result paths for the requested category, newest first, and apply the optional maximum number of results after ordering.

evidences.reason: Specifies the category, newest-first ordering, optional limit, and returned paths.
Selects JSON files and applies the result limit after sorting.

requirements.text: Load the most recent saved result in the supplied category, restricted to the requested operation when an operation is supplied. Return null when there is no matching result.

evidences.reason: Distinguishes listing and loading from retrieving the most recent result for an operation.
Defines the latest-result lookup, its optional operation filter, and its nullable return.

requirements.text: After completing and saving an analysis, read its relevant saved JSON results and create a Markdown summary in results/summaries/ with data tables, trends, and recommendations.

evidences.reason: Specifies the order of analysis, saving, and reading the saved files to create the summary, as well as the summary contents.
Identifies the dedicated location for human-readable Markdown summaries.
The general date-range section says all functions accept these formats, including GA4 relative dates.
The service-specific contract requires calendar dates for Search Console; passing a date object through does not convert GA4 relative values.
The function signatures distinguish dated reports from realtime, URL, and field-list operations without date inputs.

issues.reason: Apply the date formats only to operations that accept a date input. Use the explicit service-specific calendar-date requirement for Search Console; the general statement supplies no basis to require relative values there or date inputs on undated operations.

evidences.reason: The public contract describes dimension filters and sort order as optional controls.
The implementation reads both controls but neither reaches the API request.

issues.reason: Retain both caller-facing obligations from the explicit reference. The implementation does not currently satisfy them. The source does not fix a particular filter or sort encoding.

evidences.reason: The standalone top-pages operation is described as ranked by impressions.
The entry-point help describes that same standalone operation as ranked by clicks.
The overview promises top pages and the SEO page analysis expressly specifies clicks.
The overview uses the shared top-pages helper.
The SEO page analysis also uses the shared top-pages helper.
The query request specifies dimensions and pagination without an explicit sort.
The shared helper sets the page dimension and row cap without distinguishing the two ranking descriptions.

issues.reason: The shared helper's documented ranking is inconsistent. Preserve the common top-pages obligation and its row cap, and retain the SEO analysis's explicit click-ranking objective in that scope. The source does not determine whether the standalone and overview uses should rank by clicks or impressions, or whether the SEO use requires a distinct ranking.

evidences.reason: The description of queries with a device breakdown can indicate a breakdown within each query.
The keyword workflow calls a top-query helper and a separate device helper.
The top-query helper uses only the query dimension.
The device helper uses only the device dimension.

issues.reason: The source supports both a device breakdown for each query and separate query and site-level device views as readings of the requested analysis. Preserve the need for both views of the period without claiming that the separate reports provide per-query device values.

evidences.reason: Places a country breakdown within the page performance analysis without specifying whether it is per page.
Collects the page and country results through separate helpers.
The country helper groups by country without the page dimension.

issues.reason: The page-analysis label leaves open whether country performance must be broken down within each page or supplied as a separate site-wide view. The current separate country result supports the latter interpretation but cannot supply the former.

evidences.reason: Describes each standalone result as an array while naming MetadataResponse as the return type.
Defines MetadataResponse as an object with named dimension and metric collections.
Returns each standalone collection under its corresponding named property.

issues.reason: The explicit return type and the implementation agree on a named collection within MetadataResponse. Read the reference's array description as specifying the collection contents, not a bare array at the top level.

evidences.reason: The general workflow describes automatic saving of all results.
The custom report explicitly allows saving to be disabled.
The bulk lookup has its own optional save control.
An empty lookup returns before any request or save, even though saving defaults to enabled.
The comparison saves the combined result while expressly suppressing component saves.

issues.reason: Treat automatic saving as the default for operation results. The more specific save controls, early return without a report, and combined-artifact rules govern those cases; the general workflow does not override them.

evidences.reason: The general filename example displays an extra information segment.
The storage contract makes extra filename information optional.
The filename includes the extra segment conditionally.

issues.reason: Use the documented timestamp and operation segments and include the extra segment only when there is extra information. The storage contract and filename construction agree that it is conditional.

evidences.reason: The optional filter identifies the operation whose most recent result should be retrieved.
The implementation searches for a substring in the file path and then loads the first match, so it can select a different operation with a matching name prefix or filename segment.

issues.reason: Preserve the requested operation's identity as specified by the lookup contract. Substring matching is an implementation detail that can violate that identity.

evidences.reason: The workflow defines summarization after saving as a phase of every analysis.
The tips advise asking for a summary after pulling data and could be read as making it a separate request.

issues.reason: The explicit analysis workflow governs a completed analysis, and the tip does not impose a permission or request condition on that workflow. The workflow does not require every individual utility call to create a summary.
